findings.title: Printed degree reverses the acyclicity needed in Lemmas5.3-5.4 and Theorem5.8
findings.counterexample: Rank1 phi=p, N=0, Hodge jump0 has printed degree1; every contained jump h<=0 cannot equal tN=1. Actual bundle O(-1) has Vst=0, but claimed M* is nonzero.
findings.repair: Use degree tH-tN. Take positive HN subobject and zero-slope quotient; reduce one filtration step on positive part. Each quotient degree falls at most1 and stays>=0. Iterate total integral degree to0. Largest positive step preserves Lemma5.4 endpoints; existing period-Hom argument then applies.
findings.impact: Main geometric comparison not refuted; complete local repair relative to cited HN/admissibility inputs.

findings.title: Proposition5.23 chooses a nonexistent bounded admissible lattice
findings.counterexample: E=O(1)+O, L=Re+Rf, L0=R(e+tf)+R(t^2f); E0=O+O(-1), phi slopes0,1. For r2 all bounds hold. Unique degree0 intermediate N=Re+Rtf gives O(1)+O(-1), not weakly admissible.
findings.repair: By Theorem3.12 and BC full embedding, HomVS(Vst^r,Bk)=Hom_R(t^rL,Bk). Restriction from L0 has elementary divisors t^a,0<=a<=r; kernel/cokernel killed t^r. k0 zero,r0 iso.
findings.impact: False central proof step; conclusion survives with stronger bound.

findings.title: HN extension bullet omits bounds on both factors
findings.counterexample: Split O(2)+O(-1) with lambda1=0,lambda2=1 satisfies printed one-sided hypotheses but not claimed interval.
findings.repair: Require both factors in the interval; nonnegative extension closure used elsewhere is valid.

findings.title: Slope inequality and tensor/Hom multiplicities
findings.counterexample: Cokernel Dimension(h-d,-h) forces h>d, not printed h<d. Rank forces tensor multiplicity h1*h2/h. End(O(1/2)) has Qp-dimension4, not1.
findings.repair: Reverse final inequality; correct multiplicity and insert corresponding multiplicity in Hom formula.
findings.impact: Local formula group; equivalence theorem unchanged.

findings.title: Pure-prime-power index in Lemma4.13 is outside range

findings.repair: Use i1 if p notdiv k; p^r if k=p^r*m,m>1; p^(r-1) if pure power. Binomial valuations0,0,1. Correct b_(i,k-1) to b_(i,k-i).
findings.impact: Uniform p^-1 bound and convergence preserved;635 exact finite cases only corroboration.

findings.title: Lemma4.24 prints nonzero Ext where its proof gives zero

findings.repair: Keep Hom=W; change Ext1 to0 as already proved and used in(ii).

findings.title: Example5.11 drops twist and dual
findings.counterexample: Rank1 phi=p,Hodge jump1,r1 gives Xst^1=Qp and Hom slope0; printed M* slope-1.
findings.repair: Use M*{r}, and M_K* for j<=0. Remark9.2 already preserves the twist.

findings.title: Proposition5.20 positive-period kernel and lattice direction
findings.counterexample: Full Bst-invariant periods do not map naturally into printed positive BdR quotient. An admissible lattice supplied by Remark5.14(iii) is contained in L, not containing L.
findings.repair: Use Bst+ in positive-target kernel or full BdR target; take admissible N subset L and t^rV subset Vst^r. For5.18 choose N subset t^-rL0; do not require L0 subset N.

findings.title: Both signs in bicartesian sequence6.17 are plus
findings.counterexample: For point r0, diagonal1 composed with sum gives2 rather than0.
findings.repair: Replace the final sum by difference, or change one sign in first map.

findings.title: Filtered logarithmic de Rham group need not have finite length
findings.counterexample: Proper point gives H0(F^rRΓdR)=t^rR, free rank1 and not finite length.
findings.repair: Use finite type. Diagram surjectivity uses upper exactness and de Rham identifications, not finite length.

findings.title: Kunneth proof assigns perfectness to the wrong complex
findings.counterexample: Y point and T countable disjoint union of points give infinite-dimensional rational H0 of RΓ(T,RΓ(Y,Zp)); allowed smooth separated taut countable-at-infinity T.
findings.repair: Use perfectness of proper-factor RΓ(Y,Zp); bounded finite-projective resolution commutes with RΓ(T,-) and gives projection formula.
findings.impact: Local correction retains Kunneth under cited proper base change/finiteness.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed under the printed degree/acyclicity definitions; main geometric comparison not refuted.
per_problem.reasoning: With K=F=Qp, rank one phi(e)=p e, N=0 and Hodge jump 0, the printed degree tN-tH is 1 and the object is acyclic by Definition 5.1. Every contained filtration has jump h<=0, so it cannot be weakly admissible with h=tN=1. The r=1 bounds in Lemma 5.4 hold. The actual associated bundle is O(-1), whose H0 vanishes by (3.10); equivalently t^-1 y with y in Be intersect t BdR+ is zero. Theorem 5.8 would recover nonzero M* from zero Vst under the printed definition.
per_problem.repair_check: Changing to tH-tN also requires orienting the HN proof correctly. Take the positive-slope subobject P and slope-zero quotient Q. Every nonzero quotient of P has integral positive degree >=1; lowering a single Hodge step by a hyperplane lowers each quotient degree by at most one. Quotients remain nonnegative, total degree drops by one, and iteration yields a contained weakly admissible filtration. For Lemma 5.4 choose the highest positive step; phi-slopes >=0 ensure such a step exists and Fil0/Fil(r+1) are preserved. The existing period-Hom argument then works relative to the cited HN/admissibility inputs.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed false bounded intermediate-lattice step, with a valid stronger local repair.
per_problem.reasoning: For E=O(1) direct-sum O, R=BdR+, L=Re+Rf and L0=R(e+t f)+R t^2 f, the first-summand intersection is tRe and second-summand image tRf. Hence E0 is an extension O(-1) by O which splits because H1(O(1))=0, so its Frobenius slopes are 0,1. E is acyclic, r=2 satisfies t^2L0 subset t^2L subset L0, and all k>=4 are allowed. L/L0 is cyclic of length two, whose unique intermediate length-one lattice is Re+Rtf; its bundle O(1) direct-sum O(-1) is not semistable of slope zero.
per_problem.repair_check: Theorem 3.12 and full embedding of BCs identify HomVS(Vst^r,Bk) with Hom_R(t^rL,Bk). The displayed map is restriction from L0. Elementary divisors t^a with 0<=a<=r show both kernel and cokernel killed by t^r, stronger than t^(2r). This includes k=0 and r=0. No geometric theorem or the estimate itself is claimed false.

per_problem.reasoning: The split extension O(2) direct-sum O(-1) satisfies the printed separate lower/upper bounds with lambda1=0 and lambda2=1 but has slopes outside [0,1]. Requiring both factors in the interval repairs the recalled extension statement; nonnegative extension closure remains available.

The cokernel Dimension(h-d,-h) forces h>d, not the last printed h<d. Rank of O(lambda1) tensor O(lambda2) is h1 h2, so multiplicity is h1 h2/h. The source image actually prints (h1/h2)h. For lambda1=lambda2=1/2, the omitted Hom multiplicity gives dimension one instead of End dimension four. The equivalence theorem does not depend on retaining these recalled misprints.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed by a general valuation argument, not by finite tests alone.
per_problem.reasoning: When k=p^r the proposed i=p^r is excluded by i<k. For k>=2 choose i=1 if p does not divide k, i=p^r for k=p^r m with m>1 and p not dividing m, and i=p^(r-1) for a pure p-power. The binomial valuations are respectively 0,0,1, yielding the uniform p^-1 bound and convergence. The coefficient index is b_(i,k-i). Historical 635 tests are corroboration only and were not rerun.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed from statement and its own exact-sequence proof.
per_problem.reasoning: Lemma 4.24 prints Ext1(Ud,W)=W while its proof proves Ext1=0. For d=1,W=B1 nonzero the connecting map onto Ext1(B1,B1) is surjective, so Ext1(U1,B1)=0. Hom=W is retained; the subsequent use agrees with the corrected zero.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed; downstream twist retained as counterevidence against a main-theorem failure.
per_problem.reasoning: For phi=p and Hodge jump 1 with r=1, Xst^1=Qp and its period-Hom Frobenius slope is zero, whereas M* has slope -1. Corollary 5.10 supplies the omitted {r} twist. The de Rham answer is M_K* rather than M_K for j<=0. Remark 9.2 already has the twist.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed; do not reinstate the false stronger bounded-lattice requirement of P2.
per_problem.reasoning: Full Bst invariants have no natural period-inclusion map to the printed positive BdR quotient; use Bst+ for that target or the full BdR quotient. Remark 5.14(iii) supplies an admissible lattice contained in L, contrary to containing in the proof. Then t^rV lies in the required kernel and spans the period module. For Proposition 5.18 choose the admissible lattice inside the maximal t^-r L0, whose bundle has nonnegative slopes r minus the original Frobenius slopes; requiring L0 subset N would be unjustified.

In (6.17) both arrows use plus signs. On a point with r=0 the composite sends 1 to 2, so it is not a complex. A difference in the last map, or one negative component in the first, restores the usual exact sequence of the bicartesian square.

per_problem.verdict: Confirmed and locally harmless to the displayed conclusion.
per_problem.reasoning: For a proper point, H0(F^r RΓdR)=t^r BdR+ is free rank one and not finite length. Finite type is appropriate. The diagram's surjectivity is supplied by upper exactness and de Rham identifications and does not require the false finite-length assertion.

Taking Y a point and T a countable disjoint union of points, allowed by smooth/separated/taut/countable-at-infinity scope, makes the asserted global-section complex have infinite-dimensional rational H0 and hence not be perfect. It is RΓ(Y,Zp), the proper factor, whose finite-projective representative permits passage through RΓ(T,-). This yields the desired projection formula relative to cited proper base change/finiteness, not a Kunneth statement for two arbitrary nonproper factors.
